newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia proposes 39.4 bln kuna budget for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Croatia proposes 39.4 bln kuna budget for 1997.

text.p: Croatia's government will propose to parliament, the Sabor, a 39.4 billion kuna budget for 1997, Deputy Prime Minister Borislav Skegro said on Friday.
That budget would be up from 35.6 billion this year.
Skegro told a news conference the increase was based on an expected nominal gross domestic product (GDP) rise of rougly nine percent to 108 billion kuna.
Of a planned 35.5 billion kuna total public spending, 32.7 billion would be covered by tax and other revenues. Tax and revenue are projected to rise by 5.05 percent next year.
Croatia will borrow the difference of 6.8 billion kuna, but almost four billion will go toward repaying old debt maturing next year, Skegro said.
"The central government deficit will be 2.63 percent of GDP, which is under the 3.0-percent limit allowed by the Maastricht criteria," he said.
Due to lower than projected current expenditures, this year's budget gap is seen below the planned 2.5 percent . -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
